name: Delaware DNREC Septic Permits
_agent_notes: Written from data/profile/de_dnrec_septic.json (88,171 rows; the source itself publishes 88,183 rows for only 76,339 unique OBJECTIDs, so duplicates are upstream).
Owner names/addresses are dropped at fetch time (sources.json drop_fields).
HorizontalMethod: 74% Parcel Centroid (medium), 20% photo-interpolated from orthophotos + 4% GIS high-accuracy (high: placed on the actual system), 2% address match (medium).

PermitStatus decides whether a system exists: Void/Revoked/Withdrawn/Denied/Returned/Suspended = never built (excluded). System Abandoned = likely converted to sewer (excluded from septic; useful later as sewer evidence). Pending/On Hold/Application Received = proposed (excluded). Expired = kept as septic_unconfirmed.
16,918 parcels have multiple permits (original + replacements); one_per_parcel keeps the newest so the tank size and system type are current.
SiteAddress is only 22% filled and lacks house numbers, so it is kept as a partial address; ZIP comes from the parcel centroid.
TreatmentTankCapacity 0 means not recorded, so it is mapped to null.

Review 1: of 622 out-of-state points, some are clearly bad (e.g. a Virginia point, rejected) and some sit within tens of meters of the PA/MD line; a 150 m border tolerance now keeps those with a near_boundary flag.

Review 2: 605 of the 606 remaining rejects share one sentinel point in Virginia (37.978, -77.693) — failed photo placements. Each has a valid parcel centroid, so fallback_coords recovers them as parcel_centroid (medium confidence) with a coords_recovered_from_fallback flag.
